messages.subject: within item dimensionality and correlation
parts:
Hi Phil,

 

I am new in the group, so first of all thank you very much for the mirt package. As I said I am new in the group and using mirt package so probably the question is because of my lack of experience.

I am trying to model a depression and anxiety questionnaire (45 items). In this questionnaire several items measure both dimensions, so I have a whithin-item dimensionality. If I do an exploratory analysis asking for two dimmensions they are high correlated (.6).

The problema I found is that when I make a confirmatory analysis although I ask for the COV=F1*F2 and rotation=’oblimin’, in the output the correlation between the factors is 0. Is any way I can solve this?

 

Thanks in advance

Luis

Hi Luis,

Welcome to the group.

On Thu, Jan 22, 2015 at 6:12 AM, <lmlo...@ugr.es> wrote:


Hi Phil,

 

I am new in the group, so first of all thank you very much for the mirt package. As I said I am new in the group and using mirt package so probably the question is because of my lack of experience.

I am trying to model a depression and anxiety questionnaire (45 items). In this questionnaire several items measure both dimensions, so I have a whithin-item dimensionality. If I do an exploratory analysis asking for two dimmensions they are high correlated (.6).

The problema I found is that when I make a confirmatory analysis although I ask for the COV=F1*F2 and rotation=’oblimin’, in the output the correlation between the factors is 0. Is any way I can solve this?

Unfortunately you've stumbled across a printing bug in the current version (new version should be available in a few days which fixes this). For now, use coef() to see what the actual correlation is instead of summary(). Also, rotations are not used in confirmatory models, so the oblimin rotation is simply ignored. Cheers.

Phil
 

 

Thanks in advance

Luis
